plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: Branches fill with clouds of delicate, blush-white blossoms before the leaves emerge. Petals drift down like snow in the spring breeze. The effect is one of the most celebrated spring displays in the world.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in much of Japan. Flowering often begins in warmer areas such as Tokyo and Kyushu around March 19–25, and in Washington, D.C. it usually peaks in late March to early April.
plants.location: Japan (southern and central Honshu, Kyushu) and Washington, D.C., USA
plants.funFact: Every Yoshino cherry is a clone. All trees are grafted from a single original, so entire groves bloom in near-perfect synchrony.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: Nodding, trumpet-shaped flowers glow butter-yellow against fresh green leaves. They carpet woodlands and meadows in golden drifts. They are a cheerful sign that winter is ending.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late February to April, with peak bloom in March in the UK and western Europe
plants.location: Western Europe, including England, Wales and the Netherlands
plants.funFact: Daffodils contain toxic alkaloids such as galantamine, which has been developed into a medicine used for early-stage Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Goblet-shaped, lilac-pink blooms rise from bare soil on slender stalks. They look like crocuses, but they flower in the southern autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn. In the Southern Hemisphere that means roughly March to April.
plants.location: Cultivated in gardens in southern Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: The flowers appear without leaves. The foliage grows months later, in spring, which earned it the nickname "naked ladies."
